messages:
Maya: Quick sync — we need a final call on MVP scope for Search Assist before EOD Friday. Acme pilot pushed two asks: multi-tenant prefix cache and a light-weight response re-ranking hook. Both have infra and cost implications. Can we triage?
Tony: Can you share priority order? are both blockers for pilot or stretch?
Maya: Priority = 1) prefix cache (they need <50ms tail), 2) rerank hook is nice-to-have but they'd accept server-side rerank fallback.
Sam: From UX POV, rerank improves precision for the demo but not required for GA. We can show a fallback label and call it out in docs.
Tony: Technically, multi-tenant prefix cache means per-tenant KV namespaces + eviction. Biggest risk is memory blowup with hot tenants.
Lina: Also depends on model variant. If they use the 8k context model we can cache prefixes cheaply; with 32k we'll need different eviction heuristics.
Raj: SRE concerns: per-tenant caches increase memory fragmentation and complicate autoscaling. We'd need a reserve pool or cap + burst policy.
Maya: Understood — what's the minimal engineering work to get an acceptable pilot tradeoff?
Tony: Minimal path: single shared prefix cache with tenant tagging + strict per-tenant soft cap. No perfect isolation but keeps memory bounded. Implement in two sprints (core + safety).
Raj: Ops changes: need a new metric (tenant_cache_mem) and an alert if any tenant > 75% of pool. Also add circuit-breaker to bypass cache on high pressure.
Lina: For rerank: we can ship a server-side lightweight scoring function (logistic on features) now, and rollout ML reranker in v1. That buys time.
Sam: That works for demo. We'll add a UI toggle "Demo rerank" so PMs can switch on/off for pilot.
Maya: Ok — so proposal: include shared prefix cache in MVP with per-tenant soft caps + circuit-breaker, and defer ML reranker to v1 with server-side fallback in MVP. Any blockers?
Tony: Two small ones: 1) needs a minor schema change to request envelopes to include tenant_tag, 2) need canary plan for cache rollout.
Raj: I can own canary + metrics. Will need a checklist.
Maya: Great. Tony, can you draft the tech spec and timeline? Try to keep the core work in this sprint + one next sprint.
Tony: Will do. Drafting now, will ping for review in ~90m.
Sam: I'll prep demo copy + toggle in the staging UI once spec lands.
Lina: I'll stub a simple logistic reranker and keep data collection hooks in place for v1.
Raj: Adding ops checklist to our runbook:
```
- Add tenant_cache_mem metric
- Alert: tenant_cache_mem > 75% of pool
- Circuit-breaker endpoint /cache/bypass for emergencies
- Canary rollout: 5% traffic -> 25% -> 100% (24h windows)
- Post-canary: run memory profiler job
```
Maya: Awesome — can everyone confirm ETA: tech spec by today COB, ops checklist done by tomorrow EOD, UI demo toggle by Thurs?
Tony: Spec by COB today ✅
Raj: Ops checklist by tomorrow EOD ✅
Sam: UI toggle by Thu lunchtime (blocking on spec) ✅
Lina: Data hooks stubbed by Thurs EOD ✅
Maya: Thanks team. I'll update Acme with scoped plan: MVP = shared cache + fallback rerank, v1 = per-tenant isolation + ML reranker. Sending note after Tony's spec. :thumbsup: 
release-bot: Deployment note: staging rollout for cache-prototype scheduled for 2024-06-14 02:00 UTC. Monitor the new metric `tenant_cache_mem`.
Maya: Noted. We'll watch the canary metrics closely and regroup post-staging run.
Tony: FYI, spec link: https://redwood.internal/docs/specs/search-assist-cache (draft)
Maya: Closing thread — thanks all.
